4494-the-tale-of-chloe-an-episode-in-the.title: The Tale Of Chloe An Episode In The History Of Beau Beamish
4494-the-tale-of-chloe-an-episode-in-the.creator: George Meredith
4494-the-tale-of-chloe-an-episode-in-the.description: A book by George Meredith. The ballad of 'The Duke and the Dairymaid,' ascribed with questionable authority to the pen of Mr. Beamish himself in a freak of his gaiety, was once popular enough to provoke the moralist to animadversions upon an order of composition that 'tempted every bouncing country lass to sidle an eye in a blowsy cheek' in expectation of a coronet for her pains--and a wet ditch as the result!

arxiv-2009-09393.title: Transform Domain Pyramidal Dilated Convolution Networks For Restoration of Under Display Camera Images
arxiv-2009-09393.creator: Hrishikesh P.S, Densen Puthussery ⋆, Melvin Kuriakose, Jiji C.V
arxiv-2009-09393.description: Abstract Under-display camera (UDC) is a novel technology that can make digital imaging experience in handheld devices seamless by providing large screen-to-body ratio. UDC images are severely degraded owing to their positioning under a display screen. This work addresses the restoration of images degraded as a result of UDC imaging.

arxiv-2111-01324.title: Escape kinetics of self-propelled particles from a circular cavity
arxiv-2111-01324.creator: Tanwi Debnath 1 , Pinaki Chaudhury 1 , Taritra Mukherjee 2 , Debasish Mondal 3 and Pulak K.Ghosh 2
arxiv-2111-01324.description: Abstract We numerically investigate the mean exit time of an inertial active Brownian particle from a circular cavity with single or multiple exit windows. Our simulation results witness distinct escape mechanisms depending upon the relative amplitudes of the thermal length and self-propulsion length compared to the cavity and pore sizes.

arxiv-2408-13360.title: Symbolic dynamics of joint brain states during dyadic coordination
arxiv-2408-13360.creator: Italo Ivo Lima Dias Pinto, Zhibin Zhou, Javier O. Garcia, Ramesh Srinivasan
arxiv-2408-13360.description: Abstract We propose a novel approach to investigate the brain mechanisms that support coordination of behavior between individuals. Brain states in single individuals defined by the patterns of functional connectivity between brain regions are used to create joint symbolic representations of brain states in two or more individuals to investigate symbolic dynamics that are related to interactive behaviors.

arxiv-2505-21127.title: The TYPHOON Stellar Population Synthesis Survey. II. Pushing Full Spectral Fitting to the Limit in the Nearby Grand Design Barred Spiral M83
arxiv-2505-21127.creator: Eva Sextl, Rolf-Peter Kudritzki, Fabio Bresolin, Kathryn Grasha, Hye-Jin Park, Qian-Hui Chen (陈千惠), Andrew J. Battisti, Mark Seibert, Barry F. Madore, Jeffrey A. Rich
arxiv-2505-21127.description: Abstract We apply population synthesis techniques to analyze TYPHOON long slit spectra of the starburst barred spiral galaxy M83. The analysis covers a central square of 5 arcmin side length. We determine the spatial distribution of dust through the analysis of reddening and extinction, together with star formation rates, ages, and metallicities of young and old stellar populations.

arxiv-2507-04762.title: Robustifying 3D Perception via Least-Squares Graphs for Multi-Agent Object Tracking Thanks: This work has received funding from the EU’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme in the frame of the CoEvolution project “A comprehensive trustworthy framework for connected machine learning and
arxiv-2507-04762.creator: Maria Damanaki 1,3 , Ioulia Kapsali 1 , Nikos Piperigkos 1,2 , Alexandros Gkillas 1,2 , Aris S. Lalos 1,2
arxiv-2507-04762.description: Abstract The critical perception capabilities of EdgeAI systems, such as autonomous vehicles, are required to be resilient against adversarial threats, by enabling accurate identification and localization of multiple objects in the scene over time, mitigating their impact. Single-agent tracking offers resilience to adversarial attacks but lacks situational awareness, underscoring the need for multi-agent cooperation to enhance context understanding and robustness.

arxiv-2601-09683.title: Controlling thermal conductivity in harmonic chains with correlated mass and bond disorder: Analytical approach Journal: Physics Letters A
arxiv-2601-09683.creator: I. F. Herrera-González
arxiv-2601-09683.description: Abstract We investigate heat transport in one-dimensional harmonic chains with mass disorder and weak bond disorder, coupled at both ends to oscillator heat baths through weak impedance mismatches. The model incorporates correlations in mass disorder, in bond disorder, and between the two.

arxiv-2602-08809.title: Efficient Deep Learning for Biometrics: Overview, Challenges and Trends in Ear of Frugal AI Thanks: † Aya Zitouni and Aicha Zenakhri contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2602-08809.creator: 1 st Karim Haroun, 2 nd Aya Zitouni †, 3 rd Aicha Zenakhri †, 4 th Meriem Amel Guessoum, 5 th Larbi Boubchir
arxiv-2602-08809.description:
A 2026 arXiv research paper by 1 st Karim Haroun, 2 nd Aya Zitouni †, 3 rd Aicha Zenakhri †, 4 th Meriem Amel Guessoum, 5 th Larbi Boubchir. I
Introduction

In this paper, we address the challenge of deploying resource-intensive deep learning models for biometrics in resource-constrained real-world security applications. We provide a structured overview and taxonomy of Efficient Deep Learning (EDL) techniques, surveying the state-of-the-art methods that aim to reconcile the high computational demands of advanced models with the practical needs of scalable, secure, and responsive biometric systems.

pmc-10673517.title: Multidisciplinary Management of Sternal Osteomyelitis Due to Klebsiella aerogenes after Open Heart Surgery in a Patient with Multiple Myeloma: A Case Report and Discussion of the Literature
pmc-10673517.creator: Marco Pignatti, Giampiero Dolci, Elena Zamagni, Renato Pascale, Ottavio Piccin, Alessandro Ammar, Flavia Zeneli, Maria Elisa Lozano Miralles, Katia Mancuso, Riccardo Cipriani, Pierluigi Viale, Davide Pacini, Sofia Martin-Suàrez, Antonella d’Arminio Monforte
pmc-10673517.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Sternal wound complications following cardiac surgery, including sternal dehiscence, mediastinitis, and osteomyelitis, pose significant challenges in terms of management and patient outcomes. We present a case report highlighting the complex management of a patient who underwent open heart surgery for severe aortic valve stenosis, followed by sternal wound dehiscence and sternum osteomyelitis due to extended spectrum beta lactamase (ESBL) producing Klebsiella aerogenes. A multiple myeloma diagnosis was also suspected at the positron emission tomography (PET) scan and confirmed with bone marrow biopsy.

pmc-11322540.title: Problems in the assembly and analysis of the kangaroopox virus-NSW isolate
pmc-11322540.creator: Shin-Lin Tu, Chris Upton
pmc-11322540.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). nalysis performed on the sequence. We discuss 6 distinct areas of analysis that we believe to have serious errors. Poxviruses are an important family of viruses, many of which cause significant diseases of humans, wild and farmed animals. There are at least 11 poxvirus genera (some viruses are unassigned) and the dsDNA genomes range in size from 133 to 360 kb, with an approximate coding capacity of 1 gene/kb. Approximately 81 genes are common to all chordopoxviruses (infecting vertebrate hosts)1.

pmc-11451099.title: Frailty; Time for Global Action
pmc-11451099.creator: Yotam Weiss, Idit Matot
pmc-11451099.description: This commentary examines the study “Frailty and Its Association with Long-Term Mortality Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults Aged 75 Years and Over” by Lewis et al. The retrospective cohort study utilized data from a primary healthcare provider in Israel to investigate frailty using the Frailty Index (FI) and its correlation with long-term mortality.

pmc-11479303.title: The Effect of Tai Chi (Bafa Wubu) Training and Artificial Intelligence-Based Movement-Precision Feedback on the Mental and Physical Outcomes of Elderly
pmc-11479303.creator: Yuze Zhang, Haojie Li, Rui Huang
pmc-11479303.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). (1) Background: This study aims to compare the effects of AI-based exercise feedback and standard training on the physical and mental health outcomes of older adults participating in a 4-week tai chi training program. (2) Methods: Participants were divided into three groups: an AI feedback group received real-time movement accuracy feedback based on AI and inertial measurement units (IMUs), a conventional feedback group received verbal feedback from supervisors, and a control group received no feedback.

pmc-11515870.title: Health status by time of arrival among Ukrainian refugees in Norway
pmc-11515870.creator: A S Labberton, L Ozeryansky, Y Helland, T S Skogheim, T M Hansen
pmc-11515870.description: BackgroundOver 75000 refugees from Ukraine have come to Norway since February 2022. Previous studies show that the refugees have poor health for several domains, and reports suggest that those fleeing Ukraine at later stages have even poorer health. However, more systematic knowledge is lacking.

pmc-11646673.title: Exploring the reporting, intake and recommendations of primary food sources of whole grains globally: a scoping review

pmc-11646673.description: Keywords: Whole grain, Food sources, Whole-grain calculation, Dietary guidelines, Epidemiology Non-communicable diseases are the leading cause of death and disability worldwide and attribution continues to increase, secondary to population growth and ageing(1). Primary contributors to disease burden include CVD, cancer, chronic respiratory disease and type 2 diabetes(1).

pmc-12431454.title: Decentralized and Network-Aware Task Offloading for Smart Transportation via Blockchain †
pmc-12431454.creator: Fan Liang
pmc-12431454.description: As intelligent transportation systems (ITSs) evolve rapidly, the increasing computational demands of connected vehicles call for efficient task offloading. Centralized approaches face challenges in scalability, security, and adaptability to dynamic network conditions. To address these issues, we propose a blockchain-based decentralized task offloading framework with network-aware resource allocation and tokenized economic incentives.

pmc-12457847.title: Cost-Effective and Reproducible Preparation of mRNA-Loaded Lipid Nanoparticles Using a Conventional Laboratory-Scale Microfluidic Assembly System
pmc-12457847.creator: Yunqi Li, Min Wu, Ruoyang Zhao
pmc-12457847.description: This protocol describes a standardized and economically accessible method for synthesizing mRNA-encapsulated lipid nanoparticles using routine laboratory equipment, including precision syringe pumps, Y-shaped glass microfluidic chips, and silicone tubing. Designed to address the cost and accessibility limitations of commercial microfluidic platforms, the system achieves performance metrics comparable to high-end devices while reducing equipment costs by 90%.

pmc-12630019.title: A letter to the editor in response to the article titled “From knife to needle – the trend of vascular neurosurgery in Belgium” by Veken et al
pmc-12630019.creator: Prashant Lakhe, Alok Umredkar, B.C. Anil Kumar, Varidh Katiyar
pmc-12630019.description: vascular neurosurgery. The emphasis is correctly laid on the need to further investigate the reasons that underlie the changes in the trends. Endovascular neurosurgery has indeed revolutionized the field of cerebrovascular surgery. There should be no surprise to see a generalized inclination favouring endovascular therapies over fine microsurgical skull base techniques for cerebral aneurysms.

pmc-12636866.title: Care Left Undone Among Physicians: An Explorative Thematic Analysis
pmc-12636866.creator: Simon Dello, Ken De Smet, Walter Sermeus
pmc-12636866.description: BackgroundThe concept of care left undone has been extensively studied among nurses, limited research has examined how physicians experience and respond when care is left undone. Understanding physicians’ perspectives is needed for developing more comprehensive strategies to enhance care quality and safety.ObjectiveTo explore how physicians conceptualise, experience and manage care left undone.

pmc-12774351.title: A lignan compound regulates LPS modifications via PmrA/B signaling cascades to potentiate colistin efficacy in vivo
pmc-12774351.creator: Qiuyue Diao, Zixing Zhong, Qin Zhong, Yidan Cao, Xiaona Fan, Yujiao Liang, Huihui Zhang, Zehua Cui, Xinlei Lian, Xiaoping Liao, Donghao Zhao, Jian Sun, Hao Ren
pmc-12774351.description: There has been a substantial gap between drying antibiotic pipeline and ongoing antibiotic resistance crisis, necessitating approaches to revitalize existing antimicrobials to meet unmet clinical demand for viable treatments. Herein, a lignan compound, magnolol, was identified that profoundly potentiates colistin (CS) to eradicate Gram negative bacteria and curb the development of resistance under host-mimicking condition.

pmc-13053532.title: Assessing the diagnostic performance of MediXpar texture analysis for C-shaped canal morphology on panoramic radiographs: a pilot study
pmc-13053532.creator: Sultan Uzun, Samed Satir, Turgut Felek, Guldane Magat
pmc-13053532.description: ObjectivesThis study evaluated whether panoramic radiographs could help identify C-shaped canal configurations in mandibular first premolars and offer preliminary diagnostic indicators using the MediXpar bioinformatic platform by examining pixel density and grayscale depth, in a way that approaches the diagnostic value of cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) while minimizing radiation exposure.

pmc-13086974.title: Non-coding RNA regulation of the radiation-induced DNA damage response and its translational relevance
pmc-13086974.creator: Christine Wilson, Anmol Gaur, Priyanka Swaroop, Vaishnavi Vishwas, Sachin Kumar, Sampa Ghose, Anita Chopra, D. N. Sharma, Sameer Bakhshi, Surender K. Sharawat
pmc-13086974.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Radiotherapy outcomes are strongly influenced by the DNA damage response (DDR), a coordinated network of signalling proteins, that detects breaks in DNA, and governs DNA repair, cell cycle checkpoint activation and cell-fate decisions.

pmc-13158642.title: Association Between Perceived COVID‐19 Risk and Current Use of Any Nicotine Product Amongst Adolescents in Saudi Arabia
pmc-13158642.creator: Najim Z. Alshahrani, Abdullah M. Alarifi, Ibrahim Alasqah, Ahmed K. Shukri, Abdulrahman M. Albeshry, Mohannad A. Alzain, Abdullah Algarni, Mowffaq Mohammed Kalantan, Mohamed Terra, António Raposo, Nada Alqarawi, Sarah Almutairi, Mohamed Baklola
pmc-13158642.description: IntroductionThe COVID‐19 pandemic created a unique context for tobacco‐related risk communication amongst adolescents. This study examined the link between COVID‐19–related smoking risk perceptions and current nicotine use amongst Saudi school adolescents.MethodsData were drawn from the 2022 Saudi Arabia Global Youth Tobacco Survey, a nationally representative school‐based survey (overall response rate: 92.3%). The analytic sample included 4984 adolescents aged 13–15 years.

pmc-13232751.title: Allelic association analyses: estimation recommendations
pmc-13232751.creator: Bruce S Weir, Jérôme Goudet, J Novembre
pmc-13232751.description: We offer our perspective on the rich literature on the estimation of measures of inbreeding, relatedness, and population structure, beginning with Sewall Wright’s F-statistics and moving onto the descriptive statistics of Masatoshi Nei and Clark Cockerham before discussing recent papers.

pmc-13270797.title: Switchable reactivity of homopropargylic alcohols towards γ-arylated ketones and α-arylated tetrahydrofurans in HFIP
pmc-13270797.creator: Claire Miesch, Ewelina Krolicka, Robert J. Mayer, David Lebœuf
pmc-13270797.description: A divergent synthetic strategy to access γ-arylated ketones and α-arylated tetrahydrofurans from readily available homopropargylic alcohols and arene nucleophiles is reported. This method expands the accessible chemical space of γ-arylated ketones via a unique triflic acid-catalyzed hydroalkoxylation/ring-opening arylation sequence proceeding through a 2,3-dihydrofuran intermediate, enabled by the properties of 1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoroisopropan-2-ol (HFIP) as solvent.

pmc-13380696.title: Dexmedetomidine in Palestinian intensive care units: The first multicenter cross-sector survey of sedation practices, protocol gaps, and withdrawal challenges
pmc-13380696.creator: Isra’a Abu Eid, Malak Odeh, Mawada Doaar, Mohammad Jaber, Iyad Maqboul, Ramzi Shawahna
pmc-13380696.description: ObjectiveDexmedetomidine has emerged as an important sedative due to its ability to provide cooperative sedation while preserving respiratory drive. However, its clinical use may vary across healthcare systems, particularly in resource-limited settings. This study aimed to assess patterns of dexmedetomidine use, associated protocols, withdrawal experiences, and perceived barriers across different intensive care units in the Palestinian healthcare system.

pmc-13428457.title: Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma in a Patient With Refractory Perinephric Fluid Collection and Pleural Effusion: A Case Report
pmc-13428457.creator: Chia-Chen Lin, Chie-Fu Chiu, Lieh-Hann Lin
pmc-13428457.description: Perinephric fluid collections have a broad differential diagnosis and may be difficult to characterize by imaging or fluid analysis. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) typically presents as mass-like lesions in nodal or extranodal sites but may rarely present as isolated fluid collections. We report a 53-year-old woman with acute right flank pain after minor trauma.

uslaw-usc-t33-s912.title: 33 U.S.C. § 912 — Notice of injury or death
uslaw-usc-t33-s912.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t33-s912.description: United States Code, Title 33 (Navigation And Navigable Waters); Chapter 18 (Longshore And Harbor Workers’ Compensation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Time limitation Notice of an injury or death in respect of which compensation is payable under this chapter shall be given within thirty days after the date of such injury or death, or thirty days after the employee or beneficiary.
